title: Contract Capacity Onboarding & Allocation Checklist — Mar 2028
body:
Purpose:
A compact operational checklist and per-contract allocation matrix used during customer ramp/onboarding to Dedicated capacity. This sheet captures: committed GPU types, region placements, guaranteed vs burst pools, billing slice alignment, phasing windows, and immediate runbook actions for SRE and Account teams. Intended to be copied into customer folders and linked from the onboarding ticket.

High-level notes:
- This is a working sheet: expect churn during the first 30 days of onboarding.
- Strategy: place guaranteed capacity in customer's preferred region if possible; stage burst across secondary regions to preserve latency for spikes.
- Default SLA bucket mapping: Standard (99.5), Business (99.9), Enterprise (99.95). Confirm customer's SLA during contract kickoff.

Per-contract allocation matrix (rows = logical allocation entries). Columns: allocation_id, contract_id, customer_alias, gpu_type, committed_gpus, guaranteed_region, burst_regions, start_date, phase_end, billing_slice, throughput_SLO_rps, notes

ALLOCATION-001, CT-4729, atlas-ai, H100-80GB, 40, us-west1, [us-east4, europe-west2], 2028-03-15, 2028-06-15, monthly-100k, 120 rps, initial onboarding: enable prefix cache
ALLOCATION-002, CT-4731, lumina, A100-40GB, 16, europe-west2, [us-west1], 2028-03-22, 2028-09-01, monthly-40k, 45 rps, require KV cache retention 72h; encryption KMS configured
ALLOCATION-003, CT-4735, shoply, L4-24GB, 64, us-east4, [us-west1, asia-southeast1], 2028-04-01, 2028-07-01, quarterly-200k, 300 rps, aggressive batching enabled; notify product team about latency tail
ALLOCATION-004, CT-4740, archivex, H100-80GB-quant, 8, europe-west2, [europe-west3], 2028-03-10, 2028-12-31, monthly-8k, 20 rps, quantized variant for cost savings; fallback to unquantized in outage

Capacity phasing guidance:
- Phase 0 (pre-provision): confirm billing_slice and KMS hookups; run acceptance perf tests on sample prompt set (ticket JIRA-INFRA-ACC-09).
- Phase 1 (day 0-30): provision guaranteed pool; open monitoring dashboards with token-level cost alerts and p50/p95 latency dashboards; enable canary traffic at 1%
- Phase 2 (day 31-90): increase committed throughput to target; shift burst capacity on to folded pools; review cost delta and consider quantization expansion

Region placement logic (summary):
- Strong preference for customer-requested region when latency-sensitive (chat/interactive).
- For large batch/embedding-heavy workloads, prefer cheaper region with sufficient free slab and use cross-region caching for small hotsets.
- When allocation exceeds regional slab, propose a split: guaranteed in primary, overflow in secondary; document in contract amendment.

Billing & metering notes:
- billing_slice: determines invoicing cadence and overage rules. Attach cost model exported from Billing Sheet (link in linked_artifacts).
- Metering tag format: "contract:CT-####" + "allocation:ALLOCATION-###". Ensure token-level tagging enabled before go-live.

Immediate runbook checklist (actionable items for kickoff):
- [ ] Confirm contract signature and legal billing contact (Commercial Ops).
- [ ] Kick off infra onboarding ticket and assign SRE lead (owner: Evan Chen).
- [ ] Verify KMS/HSM key provisioning (security) and attach to allocation: CT-4729
- [ ] Reserve slab in requested region(s) via capacity API (ticket JIRA-INFRA-RESERVE-88).
- [ ] Run baseline perf tests (p50/p95) and save traces to tracing bucket: gs://redwood-onboard-traces/CT-4729
- [ ] Set up per-route tracing and test function-calling flows if relevant
- [ ] Configure cost alerts: 10%/50%/90% of monthly budget slice

Risk & mitigation log (editable):
- Risk: Primary region saturation at peak (mitigation) -> Reserve burst pools in adjacent regions and enable auto-fallback routing policy; schedule customer traffic cutover training.
- Risk: Unexpected model regresses after quantization (mitigation) -> Hold canary on small holdout eval set; rollback quantization per rollout policy.

Decision history (timestamps + owner):
- 2028-03-03 Evan Chen: Use H100-80GB by default for high-throughput interactive contracts > 32 GPUs.
- 2028-03-07 Aisha Patel: Approve 72h KV cache retention for lumina (CT-4731) to meet cold-start budget.

Notes for Account Management:
- Keep customers informed of regional limitations during the 14-day provisioning window.
- Include run-rate examples showing cost under 50/75/100% utilization for the allocated slab.

Appendix A — Quick perf checklist (copy into acceptance test doc):
1) 1000 sample prompt run generating average tokens 128, measure p50/p95 latency
2) Throughput ramp test to target rps for 30 minutes while monitoring GPU util and token errors
3) Failover test: simulate region loss and validate auto-fallback within SLO

Appendix B — Short links and tickets referenced:
- Onboarding Runbook (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Contract+Onboarding+Runbook
- Reserve API ticket: JIRA-INFRA-RESERVE-88
- Acceptance tests: JIRA-INFRA-ACC-09

End of sheet.
